findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Bind `D` to the concrete path in the AC header (e.g. `D=$J/phases/discovery.md`) instead of the self-referential `D=$D`.
evidence: `D=$D` is a placeholder assigning a variable to itself
ACs depend on it: `grep -qE '^12\. \*\*Oracle strength and contract coverage\*\*' $D`, `for f in ...; do grep -q "^- \`$f\`" $D`
Scope names the file as `phases/discovery.md`, but the header never binds `D` to it
findings.finding: The Acceptance Criteria header defines `D=$D`, which is self-referential and never resolves to a real path; every AC that greps `$D` (e.g. the #12-exists check, the schema-field loop, the count-consistency check) cannot be run verbatim because `$D` is undefined.
scenarios: An executor copies the AC block and runs it; every `$D` expands to empty, silently changing grep targets to stdin or failing

findings.checklist_item: Specify the antipattern_id vocabulary usable in fallback mode: either have the patterns.md #12 section enumerate portable synonyms for the rubric's named classes (at least fail-open-oracle and unrealistic-fault-injection) or state explicitly that in a rubric-less checkout antipattern_id falls back to the three portable ids plus a defined 'other/uncategorized' value rather than being omitted.
evidence: Approach bullet: portable patterns.md section carries '(d) the three ids below' — i.e. only fixture-mutates-foreign-state, mismatched-hardening-equivalence, unstated-policy-oracle, NOT the rubric's fail-open/unrealistic-fault-injection names.

Evidence-shape bullet: 'antipattern_id takes the code-review-tests.md name where one applies, else one of the three ids above; when no named class fits it is omitted.' — in fallback mode the rubric name is unreachable, so a real fail-open-oracle finding falls through with no id even though a class fits.
Plan Context: 'janitor also runs on repos lacking that rubric' establishes the fallback mode is a first-class supported executor path.
findings.finding: In the portable-fallback mode the plan explicitly supports (repos lacking code-review-tests.md), the antipattern_id field's value vocabulary is incomplete: the fallback patterns.md section carries only the three plan-declared ids, not the rubric's named classes (fail-open oracle, unrealistic fault injection, etc.), so a finding that genuinely IS one of those rubric classes has no id to record and the 'omit when no named class fits' rule mis-covers it (a named class fits but is unreachable).
scenarios: A janitor run on a non-rebar repo (no code-review-tests.md) discovers an absence-oracle with no producer-liveness check — exactly a fail-open oracle — and the subagent must fill antipattern_id but has no in-scope id for it.
findings.suggested_fix: In the patterns.md '## Oracle strength & contract coverage (concern 12)' section, add portable id aliases for the rubric classes the fallback must still name (e.g. fail-open-oracle, sleep-synchronized-race) alongside the three new ids, and amend the Evidence-shape rule to read 'the code-review-tests.md name where the rubric is present, else the matching portable id from patterns.md, else omitted' so the omit branch fires only when no class — named or portable — fits.
